svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: What happens to finished samples, three ways (illustration)
svg.desc: An illustrative batch of 16 samples that stop at different steps, shown at four points in time. Masked array code: every sample keeps being computed every step, so finished samples are drawn as faded, held cells that still occupy the batch. Per-thread kernel: each finished thread exits and stops computing, drawn as an empty cell, but it still occupies its lane because a warp of 32 waits for its slowest lane. Eagle with compaction: finished samples leave the active set, so later launches cover fewer cells and the active set visibly shrinks, from 16 active at the start to 4 active by the last snapshot shown.
svg.text: masked: finished, still computed every step
per-thread kernel: idle, held — a warp of 32 waits
eagle: finished, lane freed — set shrinks
